title: Swietenolide inhibits the TXNIP/NLRP3 pathways via Nrf2 activation to ameliorate cognitive dysfunction in diabetic mice.
authors: Song, Xinquan; Fan, Siwen; Gao, Yuetong; Ma, Anxin; Zhang, Xiashu; Zhou, Zihui; Zheng, Yijia; Du, Lei; Zhu, Xia
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Swietenolide通过Nrf2激活抑制TXNIP/NLRP3通路改善糖尿病认知障碍，仅涉及小分子与蛋白的分子对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Oxidative stress and inflammation play important roles in diabetic-associated cognitive dysfunction (DACD). Swietenolide (Std), isolated from the fruit of Swietenia macrophylla King, exhibits various potent pharmacological activities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-tumor properties. However, the effects of Std on DACD remains unexplored. We utilized diabetic db/db mice and the hippocampal cell line HT22 to evaluate the effects and underlying molecular mechanisms of Std on DACD. Molecular docking study, western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay analyses were conducted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms involved. We found that Std significantly improved cognitive dysfunction in diabetic mice and increased cell viability in HT22 cells under high glucose condition. The reduction in superoxide dismutase (SOD) enzamy activity and glutathione (GSH) level, along with an increase in malondialdehyde (MDA) induced by high glucose in hippocampus, were reversed by Std treatment. Furthermore, Std effectively diminished the levels of proinflammatory cytokines interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha). Importantly, Std markedly activated the Nrf2 pathway to inhibit the thioredoxin-interacting protein/NOD-like receptor protein 3 (TXNIP/NLRP3) pathways. However, the neuroprotective effect of Std was significantly weakened by Nrf2 inhibitor ML385. These results indicate that Std provides substantial protection against high glucose-induced hippocampal injury by inhibiting the TXNIP/NLRP3 pathways dependent on Nrf2, which may serve as a promising agent for attenuating DACD.
abstract_zh: 氧化应激和炎症在糖尿病相关认知功能障碍（DACD）中发挥重要作用。从大叶桃花心木（Swietenia macrophylla King）果实中分离得到的斯维替诺利德（Swietenolide, Std）表现出多种有效的药理活性，包括抗氧化、抗炎和抗肿瘤特性。然而，Std对DACD的作用尚未被探索。我们利用糖尿病db/db小鼠和海马细胞系HT22来评估Std对DACD的作用及其潜在分子机制。通过分子对接 (molecular docking) 研究、蛋白质印迹法 (western blotting)、免疫组织化学 (immunohistochemistry) 和酶联免疫吸附测定 (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) 分析来阐明所涉及的分子机制。我们发现，Std显著改善了糖尿病小鼠的认知功能障碍，并在高糖条件下增加了HT22细胞的活力。高糖诱导的海马中超氧化物歧化酶 (SOD) 酶活性降低和谷胱甘肽 (GSH) 水平下降，以及丙二醛 (MDA) 水平升高，均被Std处理逆转。此外，Std有效降低了促炎细胞因子白细胞介素-1β (IL-1β) 和肿瘤坏死因子-α (TNF-α) 的水平。重要的是，Std显著激活了Nrf2通路，以抑制硫氧还蛋白相互作用蛋白/NOD样受体蛋白3 (TXNIP/NLRP3) 通路。然而，Std的神经保护作用被Nrf2抑制剂ML385显著削弱。这些结果表明，Std通过抑制依赖于Nrf2的TXNIP/NLRP3通路，为高糖诱导的海马损伤提供了实质性保护，这可能作为缓解DACD的有前景的药物。
